title: Second norm of multilinear polynomial evaluations
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $F$ assign a real coefficient to each subset of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Suppose $X_0,\ldots,X_{n-1}$ are mutually independent real random variables on this space, each has finite fourth moment, and each has mean $0$ and second moment $1$. Then the $L^2(\mu)$ norm of the random variable $\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}} F(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i$ equals the uniform $L^2$ norm of the Boolean-cube function $x\mapsto\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}F(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}\sigma(x_i)$ and $\sigma$ is the sign encoding.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is a real coefficient family indexed by subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
The random variables $X_i$ are mutually independent
